title: Could a folded sheet of paper ever reach the Moon?
description: Laksh folds a big sheet of paper again and again, and Ruhee asks about thinner paper. The video stops on one open question, whether a stack of folded paper could ever grow tall enough to reach the Moon.
teaching_notes: One idea: a small step repeated again and again can grow far more than we expect. Watch for students who say a sheet is too thin to matter, and let every guess stand because the next videos work it out.

source: Fold a sheet as many times as you can
video_script.why: Before any power or exponent appears, the child meets the puzzle that drives the chapter: how far can repeated folding go.
video_script.substitution: Picture one thin sheet folded on top of itself again and again, with the Moon far above.
video_script.anchor: Laksh and Ruhee folding a sheet of paper at a table, with the Moon in the sky above

names.Laksh: the book's child who folds the paper and has heard it cannot be folded more than seven times
names.Ruhee: the book's child who asks what happens with thinner paper like newspaper or tissue

never_show: the number of folds that reaches the Moon
maths_rules: The book says a sheet cannot be folded more than seven times; seven is said once and no other count of folds is said or shown.
No thickness, no doubling and no number of folds that reaches the Moon is said or shown; the question is left open.
The Moon is only drawn far above; no distance is said.
video_script.design: One idea: repeated folding may grow far more than we expect. Assumes nothing. The table and the folded block stay to the end; the Moon is the open question.
